extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and contributors to Ravi Vakil's 'Foundations of Algebraic Geometry' course notes / book (students, researchers, errata reporters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy for producing, editing, and publishing the course notes / book 'Foundations of Algebraic Geometry', including errata classification, versioning, editorial scope, and reader guidance about which material is essential or optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata categorization (three categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: I am arbitrarily putting potential errata into three categories. (1) substantive errata that I think may potentially seriously confuse a significant portion of readers. (2) less essential errata that I would still like to correct. (3) potential errata that don’t meet the high bar, but which I still may make note of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author subscribes to a “less is more” philosophy of errata; substantive and less essential errata will be listed and (where appropriate) copied into users' versions. Many imperfections will be allowed to slide by; some may be saved for a hypothetical revised edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive errata (please copy into your version)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of corrections labeled 'Substantive Errata' that the author asks readers to copy into their local versions (examples include corrections such as “preserve products” -> “preserve finite products”, adding missing hypotheses, correcting displayed equations, and clarifying statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are errors that may seriously confuse readers; the author lists specific line-by-line and statement-level corrections and requests they be incorporated into personal copies. (The page contains many such concrete itemized corrections.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Less essential errata and minor edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues that shouldn’t fatally derail the reader, including minor notation errors, small textual corrections, and minor editorial clarifications; the author lists many specific small changes under this heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are allowed to be copied into personal versions; they are not treated as urgent but are still considered worth correcting. Examples include small wording changes, reference corrections, and minor formula/label fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to chapters and section numbers, not page numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Because people may use different versions, I strongly encourage everyone to refer not to page numbers, but to chapters and section numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published and preprint pdf versions have different pagination and formatting; section/chapter references remain stable across versions and avoid confusion when multiple versions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning policy: avoid multiple diverging pdfs
rubrics_metrics.description: I will likely not post another pdf version, at least any time soon, because it will be too confusing if there are two diverging versions out in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author tries to post a snapshot appropriate for publication and then minimize further posted pdf changes. Errata and comments should apply to both the published and preprint versions; the author will try to keep published and online versions close.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author's scope for accepting suggested changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The author is primarily interested in mathematical errors and significant issues that affect understanding; he is not interested in certain classes of suggested changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: not interested in LaTeX issues (margins, beautification), not interested in 'ugliness of figures' (but content of figures is fair game), typos and spacing errors are fair game, and the author will focus on things that affect many readers or are mathematical mistakes/omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starred/double-starred material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The author uses stars to indicate material that is optional or more advanced: double-starred material is to be ignored by most readers; single-starred marks the hard or troublesome parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compromise policy: star/double-star to indicate whether material is essential for the core goal (covering central material in a year). Readers are encouraged to skip double-starred bits; single-starred sections indicate where the trouble lies and may be hard going.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion / compromise principle for content
rubrics_metrics.description: If we need it, I don’t want to black-box it, and I want you to understand it, but I only need you to understand it well enough to use it and move on; if we don’t need it, no matter how wonderful it is, we should just skip it, and you can learn it on your own later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author tries to balance breadth, rigor, and length so the notes can cover a central core in a year: include things necessary for use, avoid adding material that makes the manuscript unwieldy; use stars to indicate optional additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on exercises (difficulty / recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some exercises are explicitly flagged as not recommended unless the student is truly motivated (example: 'I do not recommend trying this exercise unless you are truly motivated. See [SGA4, XVII, Prop 2.1.3] for a proof by Deligne.)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises vary in difficulty; the author will sometimes annotate exercises with recommendations and references when they are especially deep or optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication / editing process notes
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be further editing and copy-editing before a finalized published version; small mathematical tweaks can still happen during that stage. The published version will be formatted nicely and will have different pagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author thanks the publisher for stylistic advice, will coordinate edits with Princeton University Press, and will try to avoid posting interim changes that create divergent versions; readers should expect formatting differences and prefer section references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions and image handling policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The author must get permissions for everything in the published versions and will replace images when permissions cannot be obtained (example: replacing a picture of 27 lines with one by Greg Egan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing material for publication, ensure image permissions; if permission cannot be obtained, use a suitable replacement and document sources/credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of editorial work
rubrics_metrics.description: Future editing will primarily address comments and mathematical corrections; figures and the index are being redone, but the author will not prioritize layout beautification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author will implement suggestions that deal with mathematical errors, omissions, figure content, and indexing; he will not focus on LaTeX layout issues like line breaks and pagination for the posted pdf versions.
